open_points.subject: A8 SOURCE_FORMATS and SOURCE_SIGNATURES
open_points.text: | `SOURCE_FORMATS` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `JPEG`, `PNG`, `WEBP`, the format names of the image library |
open_points.question: Does `SOURCE_FORMATS` contain exactly JPEG, PNG and WEBP, or every format name known to the pinned image library; and must every member have at least one `SOURCE_SIGNATURES` row?
options: Exactly JPEG, PNG and WEBP, each with one or more signature rows
Every format known to the image library, requiring additional signature rows
Every library format, with a format having no rows treated as not matched
open_points.default_guess: Use exactly JPEG, PNG and WEBP and require at least one signature row for every member.

witness.initial: A small non-empty BMP file is present in the photo folder; the image library knows BMP, but `SOURCE_SIGNATURES` has no BMP row.
events: The owner asks the calling flow to scan the project.
outcomes: An implementation reading the value as exactly JPEG, PNG and WEBP reports `rejected` with `unsupported_format`.
An implementation reading it as all image-library formats includes BMP; with no BMP rows, it may treat “every row” as vacuously satisfied and report the file `ready`.
witness.observer: The owner through the calling flow

open_points.subject: A2 allowed decoded formats
open_points.text: The source may be of a format of the imported `SOURCE_FORMATS` constant, and only those formats are decoded.
open_points.question: How is the decoded format determined and what exact outcome applies when a file passes A1's signature check but the image library identifies or successfully decodes it as a format outside `SOURCE_FORMATS`?
options: Treat the signature match as the format decision and accept any successful decode
open_points.default_guess: Check the image library's identified format against `SOURCE_FORMATS` and fail with `unreadable_image`, because A2 exposes no `unsupported_format` result.

witness.initial: A crafted polyglot begins with an allowed signature but the pinned image library identifies and decodes it as a format outside `SOURCE_FORMATS`.
events: The owner selects the file for delivery.
A1 order 6 accepts its leading signature.
The image library identifies and decodes the source.
outcomes: One implementation refuses the photo because its decoded format is outside `SOURCE_FORMATS`.
Another implementation accepts it because the signature admission check passed and decoding succeeded.
witness.observer: The calling flow, and ultimately the Portal binary store

open_points.subject: models.ConnectionsFile and models.ConnectionEntry
open_points.text:
The file has the form of = models.ConnectionsFile: one JSON object whose
   only field `objects` maps the canonical spelling of each project id (rule 9) to a = models.ConnectionEntry,
   which holds the fields of M01 other than `project_id`, each of its type.
open_points.question: Where are `ConnectionsFile` and `ConnectionEntry` defined, and what exact JSON representation does each non-JSON domain type—especially M01's `root: path`—use?
options: Introduce the two named model schemas and encode paths as JSON strings
Validate a raw JSON mapping directly against M01-derived fields without creating those schemas
Use a structured path representation rather than a string
open_points.default_guess: Introduce the two named schemas and represent every path as a JSON string.

open_points.subject: A5 connections-file parsing
open_points.text:
one JSON object whose
   only field `objects` maps the canonical spelling of each project id (rule 9) to a = models.ConnectionEntry
open_points.question: Are duplicate JSON member names—including duplicate `objects` fields or duplicate project-id keys—rejected as a broken `ConnectionsFile`, or does normal JSON parsing choose one value?
options: Reject every duplicate member name with `FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE`
open_points.default_guess: Reject every duplicate member name as a malformed connections file.

witness.initial: The connections file contains the same canonical project-id key twice, once with a confirmed connection and once with an unconfirmed connection.
events: The owner requests a scan for that project.
The service reads and validates the connections file at the connection check.
outcomes: A last-value implementation loads the unconfirmed record and answers `CONNECTION_NOT_CONFIRMED`; reversing the entries can instead allow the scan.

open_points.subject: A8 STORED_MEDIA_TYPE and M04 media_type
open_points.question: Must every new M04 `PhotoPlacement.media_type` be set from the imported `STORED_MEDIA_TYPE` constant, and must replay validate or merely return the stored value?
options: Set every new placement's `media_type` from the imported constant and validate persisted records normally
Derive the media type independently from the encoded bytes or filename
Leave the constant unused and let later contracts choose the value
open_points.default_guess: Set every new placement's `media_type` to the imported `STORED_MEDIA_TYPE` constant; replay returns the validated stored placement.

witness.initial: A valid source is delivered and encoded as JPEG.
events: The deliverer constructs M04 after storing the prepared image.
The calling flow reads the returned placement.
outcomes: Another derives a different spelling such as `image/jpg`, or has no specified value to put in the required field.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the Portal publication integration

open_points.subject: A2 OffsetTimeOriginal validation
open_points.text:
`DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` with hours up to the imported `CAMERA_OFFSET_MAX_HOURS` constant and minutes up to 59; otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
   `DateTime`.
open_points.rule:
У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь
выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The minute threshold `59` must become a value delivered through one of the three permitted paths, such as an imported data-provider constant named by this rule.
